During the early part of the war the Hutchinson family was ordered out of the Army of the Potomac by Gen. McClellan on account of the abolition sentiments expressed in its songs. The general was apparently unable to interpret the handwriting on the wall, as long before the war was ended the entire army was enthusiastically chanting that beautiful melody to the king of abolitionists--   "John Brown's body lies moldering in the grave   And his soul is marching on." Gen. McClellan was at one time the idol of the army, as well as of the entire American people.
